archetype: urban public school with a legible main entrance and administration threshold, classroom wings, specialist teaching rooms, assembly and food-service spaces, student circulation, staff/service infrastructure, exterior activity areas and a gravity-coherent partial ruin story
ground_program: prominent public-facing main entrance with weather protection, vestibule and reception or administration control point rather than an uncontrolled opening directly into teaching space
administration suite near the principal entrance with reception, offices, records or counseling functions positioned to supervise visitor access and the primary student circulation spine
classroom wings organized around real corridors with repeated but non-identical teaching rooms, storage, sanitation and staff support rather than a decorative grid of empty cells
specialist ground-floor teaching spaces such as science, art, workshop, music or library rooms use layouts and fixtures that distinguish their instructional purpose from ordinary classrooms
cafeteria or dining space connects credibly to kitchen, dry storage, cold storage, waste handling and a service entrance without routing deliveries through student classrooms

assembly, gymnasium or multipurpose volume is structurally and spatially distinct where footprint permits, with usable entrances, support rooms and clear-span logic rather than unsupported oversized voids
student and staff sanitation blocks are placed along circulation with believable access, partitions and service adjacency instead of isolated decorative fixtures
foundation edges, stairs, ramps, retaining conditions, drainage and exterior hardscape seat the school into surrounding grade without a monolithic artificial platform
upper_program: upper teaching floors continue coherent classroom and specialist-room organization around supported corridors rather than stacking unrelated decorative rooms

at least one vertically continuous enclosed stair core lands on every occupied level with supported stairs, usable landings and uninterrupted player headroom; larger footprints should retain a second independent egress route
classrooms retain plausible teaching zones, teacher position, storage and exterior glazing relationships while avoiding copy-pasted identical furnishing patterns across the entire building

library, science, art, music or staff functions may occupy upper levels where circulation and structural spans support them, but each must remain reachable from common corridors without passing through other classrooms
mechanical, electrical, janitorial and service spaces align with credible risers, roof plant and maintenance access rather than appearing as disconnected machinery closets
roof geometry distinguishes classroom wings, larger assembly volumes and mechanical zones while maintaining drainage and structural support
windows, corridor ends and stair landings correspond to actual interior spaces so the exterior reads as the envelope of a functioning institutional building rather than a pasted facade
circulation: visitors move from the principal entrance through reception or administration before reaching general student areas, preserving a clear public-to-controlled transition
students move between classrooms, sanitation, dining, library, assembly and exterior activity areas through common corridors and stairs without routing through staff-only service rooms
staff and deliveries can reach kitchen, maintenance, refuse, storage and mechanical areas from service access without crossing the principal visitor entrance or teaching rooms
every occupied level retains a continuous player-scale route to at least one supported stair core and an exterior exit direction
larger assembly, gymnasium, cafeteria or library spaces have circulation sized and arranged for their institutional use rather than single narrow decorative doorways
damage variants must preserve at least one complete entrance-to-classroom route and one viable vertical egress path through the surviving portion of the school
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a school through surviving classrooms, corridors, administration, specialist spaces and institutional circulation rather than becoming a generic ruined civic shell

favor localized roof failure, corridor collapse, shattered glazing, fire damage, water intrusion, breached classroom walls and one major structural failure zone over repeated rectangular deletion masks
major collapse may expose stacked classrooms or a gymnasium edge, but surviving slabs, beams, walls, stair cores and debris must communicate one gravity-coherent failure story
where floors or roofs fail, associated partitions, doors, glazing, fixtures and furniture must fail consistently so unsupported fragments do not float
preserve enough intact teaching rooms, administration, circulation signage cues, cafeteria or specialist spaces for educational purpose to remain inferable during exploration
at least one stair route must remain physically continuous through the surviving occupied portion; alternate stairs may be blocked or severed only where the ruin story clearly supports it
kitchen, mechanical, sanitation and service infrastructure may be exposed by damage but must remain spatially related to the rooms and risers they served
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the structure reads immediately as an urban public school rather than an office block, hospital, apartment building or generic institutional shell
main entrance, administration, classroom wings, specialist teaching spaces, dining or assembly functions and service infrastructure form a believable educational program
classrooms and specialist rooms differ meaningfully by function while still sharing a coherent institutional construction language
stairs are vertically supported, land on real floors and provide continuous player-scale headroom to every surviving occupied level
student circulation remains legible and does not require passage through kitchens, mechanical rooms, private offices or unrelated classrooms
the principal ruin exposes coherent school anatomy and gravity-driven damage rather than arbitrary missing cubes
at least one complete entrance-to-classroom route and one viable vertical egress route survive the damage state
the school meets surrounding grade through believable entrances, stairs, ramps, retaining edges and hardscape without floating foundations or buried public access
